_help: Customer-support policy for Lumen Cloud. Every threshold has a one-sentence why for the demo.
on_ezio_failure_why: If Ezio cannot be reached or returns a malformed body, public-knowledge claims were not checked, so a clean company-data check still holds instead of sending; a contradicted price or policy still blocks.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN may send only after company data agrees; YELLOW is mixed risk a manager should see; RED means Ezio already found a serious problem, so the email does not go out.

tone.why: A support email can be warm, but hype and guarantees drop tone well below 60 while the overall tier stays green, and those still need a manager.

bias.why: One strong adjective is normal; two or more one-sided phrases put bias under 70 and the draft should be rewritten before a customer sees it.

agreement.why: A single polite agreement scores about 75 and sends, but stacked flattery or agreeing with a customer's incorrect claim drops agreement to 50 or below and must go to a manager.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Not scored means Ezio found no public claim to check. Company files still gate prices and policies, and an email with nothing to check is safe to send.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: The fact-check service was down, so laws and other public claims were not reviewed. Hold unless company data already shows the draft is false, in which case block.
